qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:
EUR 25 billion to be invested in North Africa while the energy transition in Romania remains underfunded

I welcome the Commission’s efforts to strengthen strategic partnerships in the Mediterranean region through the Pact for the Mediterranean, but note that the updated action plan provides that EUR 25 billion will be mobilised through the T-MED initiative for electricity grids, renewable energy sources and clean technologies in the partner countries in the southern Mediterranean. At the same time, countries in central and eastern Europe are having to pay huge transition costs and cut back their regional development allocations in order to meet the climate targets imposed by Brussels. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.
From which headings and financial instruments do the direct contribution and the risk guarantee support for these investments totalling EUR 25 billion come?

How does the Commission justify giving huge guarantees for electricity grids in third countries at a time when eastern European Member States are having to eat into their own development funds in order to modernise their grids?

What specific assurances can the Commission provide that these external investments will not create unfair competition for energy producers in Romania and the region, who are shouldering the full costs of the green certificate system?
